## Scope and upstream basis

Skill: delivery-review. The primary delivery package is docs/plans/2026-09-08-unify-review-closeout-policy.md, bound in structured subjects. Upstream design-review is approved/current on review-closeout sha256:9d7fa84c51669929ea3aa19562fea164b5ff40788ae43f3fd98c2c7a91c26e4c and workflow sha256:7e67c59e36a938b9cb2126001deb0a951b3f91933b65bda8b24dcceafa0d72c6. Current context shows no open review findings or blockers. Retained origin drift is historical evidence and does not retarget current Design approval. This assessment read the complete plan and checked its allocation against that exact previously reviewed Design.

## Sequencing and verification judgment

Traceability: pass. RC-SR-01–04/08–10 map to M1 reviewer applications and TG-1 semantic scenarios; RC-SR-05–07/13–15/18 map to reliance, correction, failure and environment evidence; RC-SR-11/12 map to planning and consumer checkpoint behavior plus the separate M2 assessment; RC-SR-16/17 and WF-SR-16 map to consumer disposition inventory, packaging and final cross-consumer review. Together M1 and TG-FINAL-1 cover all RC obligations and the affected Workflow consumption responsibility. Retained Workflow model conventions and storage dependencies are not spuriously implemented.

Sequence and intermediate safety: pass. One coherent implementation milestone is justified by the need to avoid mixed policy across consumers; its source/resource groups remain inspectable within a bounded diff. M1 requires exact Design/Delivery authority, focused proof before adoption, canonical-first packaging, consumer inventory and independent milestone review. M2 is explicitly lifecycle-closeout, with M1 and required corrections complete before a separate fresh final whole-change Code Review. Verify follows that judgment; PR follows applicable successful Verify under the user's separate authorization. Engineering corrections return to M1 and renew the affected final assessment.

Proof adequacy: pass. TG-1 explicitly records expected versus observed installed guidance and scope limitations, with independent semantic assessment instead of text matching or transcript scoring. The named walkthroughs cover ordered judgment overlap, partial evidence with a defect, optional notes, same-author reset, bookkeeping plus failed proof, changed final subjects, Verify-owned blockers, concurrent basis changes, interrupted recording, changed proof environment and missing final checkpoint. TG-2 assigns existing skill/build/adapter checks, and the final group adds selected repository checks and whole-change review. Existing adapter tests include archive parity and clean-install mapped-resource checks. File inventory disposition and exact subjects are required evidence, preventing a directory list from being treated as completion.

Boundary/risk coverage: pass. All eight Design dimensions have a concrete path: decision/scope inputs through scenarios; lifecycle/final review through M2 and missing-checkpoint proof; independence and authority through reset/blocker scenarios; composition/portable paths through installed-resource walkthroughs and archives; temporal/evidence changes through reuse/drift scenarios; recovery through interrupted recording and correction; compatibility through historical consumer dispositions; environment through installed resources and proof-environment change. No judgment engine, storage migration or schema change is introduced. Unmapped policy returns to Design; allocation gaps cannot be silently deferred to Verify.

Recovery and feasibility: pass. Before adoption the coherent consumer set can be restored; after reliance, stop affected continuation and fix forward without rewriting historical records. Actual system architecture location is explicitly to be resolved before editing, rather than treating the illustrative path as authority. Exact command/base/head resolution and observation of actual results prevent command placeholders from becoming proof.

## Validation inspection and limits

Checked build-adapters.py --help and validate-adapters.py --help against the plan arguments, ci.sh supported mode/base/head/jobs flags, and adapter-distribution test coverage for archive parity and installed mapped resources. These were read-only command/interface inspections; no execution, adapter build, code correctness or final verification is claimed by this Delivery Review. The plan's v0.1.5 archive version is a local test label, not the current release version or publication authority; integrated repository checks must still validate the current support surface.

## Recording and handoff

The explicit v2 profile records this plan-centered judgment through primary review.record with current applicability. It does not invoke historical package settlement or alter engineering subjects or routing. The approved scope is sequencing and verification adequacy for authorized implementation; it does not claim completed implementation, Code Review, Verify, PR or release readiness. Return control to the coordinating actor for the user-authorized continuation.

## Independent allocation rereview

The complete revised plan explicitly allocates scripts/validation_selection.py and scripts/artifact_lifecycle_validation.py with their existing regression suites. The correction dispatches the selected v2 JSON root to existing complete-set structural validation instead of synthesizing a v1 YAML path; malformed/unknown contracts must reject, historical dispatch must remain intact, and no semantic readiness enforcement, schema or CLI interface is added. This is compatibility implementation needed for the approved v2 validation boundary, not a new policy decision. The plan includes both test-select-validation.py and test-artifact-lifecycle-validator.py and retains integrated selection checks. These checks must exercise actual combined plan-index/JSON selection, supported historical paths and unknown/malformed failure paths. Concrete implementation is still subject to independent Code Review.

Allocation, sequencing and proof adequacy remain sufficient on this revised plan. The earlier no-finding assessment remains applicable to unchanged allocation, after rereading the complete plan and current exact Design references. No open Delivery finding or necessary owner decision was identified. M1 Code Review is still pending; this renewed Delivery judgment does not approve its implementation or the unimplemented compatibility fix. Return control to the implementation coordinator under existing user authority.
independence_basis: A separate delegated agent conducted this delivery assessment. It did not author or edit the plan or implementation; earlier participation was independent proposal and Design review only. It read the full plan, exact approved Design basis and relevant proof interfaces before judgment.
